title: Clean Multiline Text Ellipsis
explanation: Truncates long text gracefully after exactly 3 lines (or any specified number) with a native ellipsis (...) without cutting off halfway through letters.
tip: Works reliably across all modern evergreen browsers including iOS WebKit and Android Chromium.

title: Fluid Responsive Typography via clamp()
explanation: Calculates font sizing dynamically without requiring multiple media query breakpoints. Sets minimum bound (1.125rem), fluid scaling formula based on viewport width (vw), and strict upper ceiling (2.25rem).
caveat: Always combine viewport units with rem/em units (e.g. 0.95rem + 1.25vw) so users who zoom their browser font sizes maintain accessible text scaling.

title: Fluid Responsive Typography with Clamp
explanation: Calculates font size dynamically based on viewport width: never shrinks below 1.25rem (min), scales proportionally on mid-size screens, and caps at 3rem (max) without media queries.
tip: Combine rem with vw units to ensure users who adjust their browser base font size still see accessible scaling.

title: Frosted Glassmorphism Effect
explanation: Creates a modern frosted-glass container using semi-transparent alpha backgrounds and hardware-accelerated backdrop blur with a subtle light-catching border.
tip: Always test contrast ratios for text placed on top of blurred dynamic backgrounds for accessibility.

title: Hide Scrollbar (Keep Scrolling)
explanation: Removes visual scrollbars while preserving touch, trackpad, and mouse-wheel scrolling across Chrome, Safari, Firefox, and Edge.
tip: Ensure content still has visual cues (like gradients or shadows) so users realize the area is scrollable.

title: Hide Scrollbars While Preserving Scroll Functionality
explanation: Completely hides visible scrollbar bars across Chrome, Safari, Edge, and Firefox while keeping elements fully scrollable via touch, trackpad, and mouse wheel.
caveat: Ensure visual indicators (like gradient fade masks) hint to users that additional content overflows beyond the visible viewport boundary.

title: Responsive Auto-Fitting Grid Without Media Queries
explanation: Creates a flawless fluid grid where cards wrap naturally as screen space allows. The min(100%, 320px) guard prevents unwanted horizontal overflow on ultra-narrow mobile displays.
caveat: Use auto-fill instead of auto-fit if you prefer empty column slots on wider screens rather than stretching few items to full screen width.

title: Attach Interactive Shell to Running Container
explanation: Spawns an interactive pseudo-TTY session inside the target container. Using /bin/sh is safer than /bin/bash as minimal base images (Alpine, distroless) rarely include bash.
caveat: If debugging a non-root container with permission locks, append --user root to elevate inside the temporary debug shell.

title: Get Running Container Internal IP
explanation: Extracts the internal bridge network IPv4 address assigned to a running container without needing to dump and scroll the full JSON inspect output.
tip: Replace <container_name> with the container's nickname or its 12-character hexadecimal ID.

title: Nuke All Dangling Docker Resources
explanation: Removes all stopped containers, all networks not used by at least one container, all unused images (not just dangling ones), and all build cache and anonymous volumes.
tip: WARNING: This will reclaim gigabytes of disk space but forces redownload and rebuild on your next run.

title: Prune All Unused Containers, Networks & Dangling Images
explanation: Removes all stopped containers, all dangling and unreferenced images, unused bridge networks, and all orphaned anonymous build cache volumes in a single sweep.
caveat: This will wipe local database containers if they use anonymous volumes. Ensure critical data is mapped to persistent named volumes or host directory mounts.

title: Stream Live CPU, RAM & I/O Metrics for Containers
explanation: Outputs a live streaming terminal dashboard showing real-time CPU percentages, memory limits, and socket network throughput for all active containers.
caveat: Omitting the --no-stream flag keeps the terminal open continuously. In CI/CD headless scripts, include --no-stream to take a single snapshot reading.

title: Discard All Local Uncommitted Changes
explanation: `git restore .` reverts all tracked modified and deleted files to HEAD, while `git clean -fd` forcefully removes all untracked files and directories.
tip: Run `git clean -nd` first to perform a dry run and inspect what would be deleted.

title: Interactive Squash of Last N Commits
explanation: Opens an interactive editor allowing you to combine the last 4 commits into a single cohesive commit. Replace 'pick' with 'squash' (or 's') on secondary commits to merge them into the previous commit.
caveat: Never rebase commits that have already been pushed to a shared production or protected branch, as this rewrites public Git commit hashes.

title: Prune All Merged Local Branches
code: git branch --merged | grep -v '\*\|main\|master' | xargs -n 1 git branch -d
explanation: Lists branches already integrated into your current branch, filters out your active branch and main/master, and cleanly deletes each merged branch.
tip: Use -D instead of -d if you need to force-delete branches with unmerged squash commits.

title: Prune Stale Remote-Tracking Branch References
code:
git fetch --prune --all
git branch -vv | grep ': gone]' | awk '{print $1}' | xargs git branch -D
explanation: Fetches updates while removing dead remote references, then locates and force-deletes all local tracking branches whose remote counterparts have already been merged and closed.
caveat: The second command uses git branch -D which forcibly deletes. Ensure you have pushed any pending commits before executing.

title: Recover Lost or Discarded Commit via Reflog
code:
git reflog | grep -E "commit|checkout" -m 5
git checkout -b recovery-branch <commit-hash>
explanation: Git keeps a chronological ledger (reflog) of every HEAD update, even for deleted branches or commits dropped by git reset --hard. Locating the hash allows instant recovery into a branch.
caveat: Reflog entries expire after 90 days for reachable commits and 30 days for unreachable commits by default, or after git gc runs.

title: Stash Staged Changes Only
explanation: Introduced in Git 2.35+, the --staged flag instructs git stash to shelve only files currently in the index (staging area), leaving unstaged workspace modifications untouched.
caveat: Requires Git version 2.35 or newer. For older Git versions, you must stash everything and selectively reapply unstaged differences.

title: Undo Last Commit (Keep Changes)
explanation: Rolls back your commit history by 1 commit, but leaves all modified files staged in your index so you can re-commit with changes.
tip: Use --mixed (the default) to unstage the files, or --hard to destroy the commit and all uncommitted code.

title: Undo Last Commit (Preserve Changes)
explanation: Moves HEAD back by one commit while preserving all modified files in your staging area. This allows you to re-stage, alter the commit message, or adjust your changes before committing again.
caveat: Do not use --hard unless you intend to permanently delete all modified code and uncommitted work in the current branch.

title: Async Sleep / Delay Promise
explanation: Provides a clean, promise-based pause mechanism within any async function, simulating network latency, polling pauses, or sequential visual transitions.
tip: Never use blocking synchronous while-loops for delays in JS; they freeze the main UI execution thread.

title: Debounce Higher-Order Function with Clean Types
explanation: Postpones the execution of an expensive callback until after a specified period of inactivity has elapsed. Essential for search auto-complete inputs, window resizing, and scroll tracking.
caveat: Preserves the 'this' context by avoiding an arrow wrapper on the returned function. Remember to cancel timers in React useEffect cleanup routines.

variations.label: Immediate (leading-edge) execution
variations.code: function debounceImmediate(fn, delay) { /* executes immediately then cools down */ }

variations.label: Throttle equivalent (at most once per N ms)
variations.code: function throttle(fn, limit) { /* enforce max execution frequency */ }

title: Deep Clone Complex Objects with structuredClone
explanation: Modern web browsers and Node.js (17+) natively support structuredClone(). Unlike JSON.parse(JSON.stringify()), it natively duplicates circular references, Dates, Sets, Maps, RegExps, and TypedArrays.
caveat: Cannot serialize functions, DOM nodes, or symbols (throws DataCloneError). For objects with methods, use specialized copy constructors.

title: Minimal Modern Debounce Function
explanation: Delays invoking a callback until after a given number of milliseconds have elapsed since the last time the debounced function was invoked.
tip: Ideal for search input typing listeners, window resize handlers, and auto-saving form drafts.

title: Native Deep Object Clone
explanation: Standard native browser API that deeply clones complex objects, preserving nested structures, Date objects, Maps, Sets, and circular references without lodash.
tip: Note: Cannot clone Functions, DOM nodes, or object prototypes; throw an error if attempted.

title: Robust Async Promise Retry with Exponential Backoff
explanation: Guarantees network and API resilience against transient rate-limits (HTTP 429) and network blips by doubling the delay period after each failed execution attempt.
caveat: Do not retry non-idempotent operations (such as credit card checkout charges) unless idempotency keys are supported by the downstream endpoint.

variations.label: Add random jitter to prevent thundering herd
Retry only on specific HTTP status codes

title: Color-Filtered Live Log Streaming
explanation: Follows log output in real-time, buffering line-by-line so outputs appear immediately when errors or warnings are thrown.
tip: Pipe into `grep --color=always` or install `ccat`/`bat` to highlight matching log levels in bright red and yellow.

title: Fast Recursive Text Search Excluding Artifacts
explanation: Recursively searches directories for the string 'SECRET_KEY', reporting line numbers (-n), skipping binary files (-I), and excluding heavy bloat folders like node_modules and .git.
caveat: For massive codebases, ripgrep (rg) or ag (The Silver Searcher) will execute significantly faster than GNU grep.

title: Identify Process Listening on Specific Port
explanation: Lists the exact Process Name and PID currently occupying port 8080. The -P flag prevents port name resolution (keeps numeric 8080) and -n avoids DNS lookups for instant results.
caveat: If lsof is not installed on lightweight Linux images, fall back to modern ss or legacy netstat commands.

title: Kill Any Process Hogging a Port
code:
npx kill-port 3000
# or natively:
lsof -ti:3000 | xargs kill -9
explanation: Finds the Process ID (PID) holding a TCP port (e.g. 3000, 8080) and terminates it immediately without having to manually search `ps aux`.
tip: Substitute 3000 with whatever port your stubborn local server (Vite, Next.js, Flask) refused to surrender.

title: Locate Top 10 Largest Files in Filesystem
explanation: Scans the root mount while staying within the same filesystem (-xdev) to avoid network mounts, finds files over 100MB, prints human-readable sizes, and displays the top 10 space hogs.
caveat: Requires sudo permissions to inspect protected system directories such as /var/log or /root.

title: Convert camelCase to kebab-case
explanation: Finds transitions between lowercase/numbers and uppercase letters and inserts a hyphen between them, then converts the result to lowercase.
tip: Great for converting React component names or JavaScript object keys into CSS class names or URL slugs.

title: Convert Text to Clean URL Slug
explanation: Sanitizes text by stripping punctuation and special characters, collapsing whitespace/underscores into single hyphens, and trimming leading or trailing dashes.
caveat: For non-Latin characters (accents/diacritics), normalize first with `.normalize('NFD').replace(/[\u0300-\u036f]/g, '')` before running regex.

title: Match and Extract Valid HTTPS Web URLs
explanation: Extracts protocol-bound web addresses from raw text strings, supporting subdomains, standard top-level domains (TLDs), ports, query strings, and URI fragments.
caveat: URL validation via regular expressions is notoriously prone to edge cases. In JavaScript applications, consider pairing this with the native new URL(string) constructor.

title: Match HTTP/HTTPS URLs with Paths
explanation: Detects web URLs starting with http or https, matching domain names, ports, query strings, and deep path structures.
tip: Use the 'g' (global) and 'i' (case-insensitive) flags when parsing long markdown or plain text documents for links.

title: Practical Email Address Validation
explanation: Validates realistic email syntax: user handles with alphanumeric and common symbols (+, ., _, -), valid domain strings, and a top-level domain of at least 2 characters.
tip: Real-world production validation should still rely on sending a verification token; RFC 5322 regexes are hundreds of characters long and often over-restrictive.

title: Strict Semantic Versioning (SemVer 2.0.0)
explanation: The official regular expression defined by the SemVer 2.0.0 specification. Accurately validates MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH versions, along with optional pre-release tags (-alpha.1) and build metadata (+20230101).
caveat: Disallows leading zeros in numeric identifiers (e.g. 1.02.3 is invalid), adhering strictly to specification rules.

title: Validate Strict ISO 8601 UTC Timestamps
explanation: Validates standardized UTC and timezone-offset timestamp representations (e.g. 2026-09-30T10:15:30Z or 2026-09-30T15:45:00+05:30) with optional millisecond fractions.
caveat: Validates format structure only; it will not catch impossible calendar dates like February 31st. For full calendar logic, pair with date-fns or native Date validation.

title: Find and Group Duplicate Records in Table
code:
SELECT email, COUNT(*)
FROM users
GROUP BY email
HAVING COUNT(*) > 1
ORDER BY count DESC;
explanation: Aggregates rows sharing the same value and filters out unique items using HAVING COUNT(*) > 1, isolating duplicate entries before applying deduplication scripts.
caveat: WHERE filters rows before grouping occurs, while HAVING filters aggregated group results after grouping.

variations.label: List full rows using window function
variations.code: SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY email ORDER BY id) as rn FROM users;

variations.label: Delete duplicates keeping lowest id
variations.code: DELETE FROM users WHERE id NOT IN (SELECT MIN(id) FROM users GROUP BY email);

title: Find Duplicate Records Across Columns
code:
SELECT email, COUNT(*)
FROM users
GROUP BY email
HAVING COUNT(*) > 1
ORDER BY count DESC;
explanation: Aggregates rows grouped by a unique column (e.g. email or username) and filters with HAVING to display only values that occur more than once.
tip: Use a CTE with `ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY email ORDER BY created_at)` if you need to selectively delete the older duplicates.

title: PostgreSQL Upsert with ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE
code:
INSERT INTO user_preferences (user_id, theme, updated_at)
VALUES ('u_9281', 'dark', NOW())
ON CONFLICT (user_id)
DO UPDATE SET
  theme = EXCLUDED.theme,
  updated_at = NOW();
explanation: Atomically inserts a new record or performs an update if a unique constraint or primary key conflict exists on the target column, avoiding race conditions in concurrent write workloads.
caveat: The target column(s) inside ON CONFLICT must have a corresponding UNIQUE constraint or PRIMARY KEY index defined on the table schema.

variations.label: MySQL equivalent
variations.code: INSERT INTO ... ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE theme=VALUES(theme);
